maya: 1812345678 — FYI escalation from ACME (ticket INC-12345). They report markdown/code-fence rendering broken immediately after today's canary rollout. Customer included repro and raw output.

maya: Request they sent (redacted):
POST /v1/generate
Headers: Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>
Payload:
{
  "model": "redwood-2.1-large",
  "prompt": "Write a Python function that adds two numbers:\n```python\ndef add(a, b):\n    return a + b\n```\nExplain briefly.",
  "stop": ["\n```"],
  "temperature": 0.0
}

maya: Customer expected generation to stop before the closing fence. Instead the response included extra fence fragments and trailing tokens. Example response (customer copy):
```text
Here's the function:
```python
def add(a, b):
    return a + b
```
```diff
+ // extra tokens here
```
(ended)
```

maya: They said this began right after rollout at ~2026-03-15T18:25:00Z. Ticket has request_id 0a1b2c3d4e and a small repro curl.

leo: Can you paste the request_id and exact bytes of the stop field? Which environment (hosted/dedicated)?

maya: request_id: 0a1b2c3d4e. Hosted API, org=acme-integ, region=us-west-2. Stop bytes are literal backslash-n + triple-backtick ("\n```").

deploy-bot: rolling-deploy/redwood-2.1 -> canary completed. rollout window: 2026-03-15T18:24:52Z -> 2026-03-15T18:27:10Z. Note: PR #4928 changed stream-stop logic.

raj: @maya thanks for the details. Looking at PR #4928 — it moved stop matching to operate on tokenized output to avoid expensive string scans. My suspicion: when a stop seq crosses token boundaries ("\n```"), we now check matches after detokenizing subtoken streams, and our detokenizer seam heuristics can insert or duplicate fence fragments. That can lead to extra backticks appearing or partial fences being emitted before the stop is applied.

sam: Can you reproduce locally against the canary model with the same stop? If yes capture raw token ids and both pre- and post-stop detokenized outputs.

maya: Repro steps I ran (curl):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-2.1-large","prompt":"Write a Python function...\n```python\ndef add(a,b):\n    return a+b\n```,"stop":["\n```"],"stream":false}'
```

maya: Output I got (raw copy):
```
Here's the function:
```python
def add(a,b):
    return a+b
```
```\n```   <-- extra tokens show up as escaped newlines + extra fence
```

olivia: I'm adding a temporary routing rule to send acme-integ traffic to the stable variant (redwood-2.0-large) and pausing the canary. Doing that now.

deploy-bot: traffic-split updated: acme-integ -> stable at 2026-03-15T18:33:12Z

raj: Thanks @olivia. I pulled canary logs and found cases where tokenizer emits two tokens that detokenize into repeated triple-backticks. I'm preparing a hotfix to: 1) apply simple ascii stop matching on the raw UTF-8 stream for short stop sequences (fences, punctuation), and 2) add tests for overlapping/fragmented stops. That should prevent duplication while keeping token-level optimizations for longer stops.

leo: Customer updated the ticket confirming that routing to stable removed the visible regression. They're okay with a short maintenance window to push the fix.

sam: Plan: ship the hotfix to canary, run a 30-min canary smoke, then resume rollout. ETA ~6 hours. @raj please confirm PR + test vectors posted here.

raj: Confirmed. I'll push patch + integration tests, and include the failing request_id (0a1b2c3d4e) as a regression test.

maya: I'll update CS and schedule a follow-up with ACME tomorrow morning. Ticket: https://tickets.redwood.ai/INC-12345

olivia: Incident status: mitigated (customer traffic routed). Will draft postmortem and include timeline + root cause when known.

maya: (reaction :thumbsup:)
